knowledge.statement: startRecoveryForInstance places the recovering replica's own state into lb.prepareReplies as a PrepareReply whose VBallot is the newly tried recovery ballot (inst.vbal is overwritten with lb.lastTriedBallot), while its Status/Command come from the recovering replica's own instance, which for a replica that never pre-accepted is Status NONE with Cmds nil.
knowledge.conditions: Any call to startRecoveryForInstance (epaxos/epaxos.go:1127-1168), including calls made from executeCommands for uncommitted instances up to crtInstance[q] after COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD (epaxos/epaxos.go:404-417).

knowledge.statement: handlePrepareReply adopts a reply's Command/Seq/Deps/Status only when reply.VBallot >= the running candidate ballot, starting from lb.ballot = the pre-recovery local vbal and evaluating the coordinator's own self-reply first; replies whose VBallot is below that running value leave lb.cmds/lb.status unchanged. lb.status == NONE then selects sub-case 6, which calls startPhase1 with state.NOOP() because lb.cmds is nil.
knowledge.conditions: Recovery of instance (replica, instance) by a replica whose own state has no pre-accepted command, when all remote replies carry a value ballot below the coordinator's freshly tried ballot (epaxos/epaxos.go:1236-1313).

knowledge.statement: Recovery of an instance by a replica that does not hold the instance's command can decide a value different from the value another live replica has already committed for that instance: the fabricated self value ballot lets the recovering coordinator adopt its own empty state, so it re-proposes a NOOP, and that NOOP is then committed at the recovering quorum while the earlier holder keeps its committed command.
knowledge.conditions: N=5, F=2 EPaxos configuration of the captured snapshot with Thrifty on and IsLeader false at the recovering replica; the instance owner fails inside its accept window (after broadcasting Accept or after the first Commit of its broadcast), the recovering replica holds the instance without its command, and the executor retries the recovery (epaxos/epaxos.go:404-417) after the first attempt.

replies below the running candidate ballot leave lb.cmds/lb.status unchanged, so sub-case 6 fabricates a NOOP

interpretations.rationale: (Reinstated complete account with the knowledge references refreshed to the current revisions of the entries it relies on; no measurement or judgment changes.) A recovery driven by a replica that does not itself hold the command replaces the value carried by its prepare replies with a NOOP, and the replacement is executed to a completed contradiction of a value another live replica has committed. Witnesses: receipt 143e14592eea4c42b3c81044e3860348 (fixed experiment fc825b4d2a9c488e8c03dff32b05cab7-experiment) - accepted value X at ballot 0 replaced, fabricated self VBallot 8 shadowing the genuine reply at value ballot 0, sub-case 6 selecting startPhase1 with state.NOOP(), holder losing X (comparison 1 violated, witness 20); receipt d80cbfd9f9a547639811aeacb19c0a30 (successor fixed experiment d9390caf51ee413aaf05a733db9b99ff-experiment) - owner commits X (index 6), Commit reaches only replica 2 (index 10) which then holds X COMMITTED (index 11), replica 3 recovers without the command, its prepare reply from replica 2 reports X with Status COMMITTED (index 16), the recovery emits the NOOP (index 19), the first attempt stalls (index 21), the executor's retry dispatches (index 24) and commits the NOOP at replicas 3 and 4 (indices 25 and 27) while replica 2 keeps X (index 26) - two live replicas holding different decided values for instance (0,0), the agreement violation this mechanism produces (comparison 0 violated, witness 25). Mechanism: startRecoveryForInstance sets lb.ballot to the pre-recovery local vbal and then overwrites inst.vbal with the freshly tried ballot (epaxos/epaxos.go:1145, 1150-1153), so the self reply outranks the genuine reply at value ballot 0 and the adoption loop (epaxos/epaxos.go:1239-1246) keeps lb.cmds nil and lb.status NONE. Recorded knowledge used: the fabricated self reply and the ballot-gated adoption (aa497fcd14934325ba2eabe45fefecd1-knowledge-0 revision 2, -knowledge-1 revision 2) and the status-guard interaction (cbbf11dd38d843f1b6acf52fd5b6e82e-knowledge-0 revision 3), summarised in the Fact ed76b573b9fe4bde9565d4b4678cda85-knowledge-0.
counterevidence: The defect is bounded to coordinators that lack the command, and that bound is executed: control experiment 242eaa8afa384a87b0952fbcd4b074b4-experiment (receipt 9d07449105684a498113db891da025d9) replayed the value-adoption crash pattern with the recovery driven by replica 2, which holds X; its preservation comparisons hold, evaluating indices 17 and 19-20.

Event 16 of receipt 143e14592eea4c42b3c81044e3860348 shows the adoption is a ballot ordering, not a general discard: a reply whose value ballot exceeded the coordinator's own recovery ballot would still be adopted.

The committed peer keeps its value in its own state: replica 2 ignores the recovered PreAccept and the recovered Commit because its instance is already COMMITTED (epaxos/epaxos.go:1082 and the Cmds-nil branch of epaxos/epaxos.go:807), so the contradiction is between two replicas' decided values rather than a silent rewrite at the holder.

The countervailing ballot-climb path in makeBallot (epaxos/epaxos.go:439-451) is gated on IsLeader, which is false in all these executions and in epaxos.New; the master-designated leader's behaviour was excluded from the scopes and is treated in the separate recovery-authority question.
limitations: One configuration and one instance in all three receipts: N=5, F=2, instance (0,0), one PUT command (key 1) and the NOOP the recovery generates.

The harness schedules delivery explicitly: the startRecoveryForInstance calls are the functions the executor invokes after COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD (epaxos/epaxos.go:404-417), but no run() loop or executeCommands goroutine was active, and the crash points were chosen by the harness within the target's permitted failure model.

The completed contradiction required the executor's retry to be invoked a second time by the harness; the contradiction itself was measured, but the executor's own retry cadence was modelled rather than run.

The premise that an accept broadcast reaches a replica that never pre-accepted uses the target's Alive mechanism between the pre-accept and accept broadcasts; a real connection loss was not exercised.
Incidental observation not used by the claim: the recovered committed instance carries Seq -1 at replicas 2, 3 and 4 while startPhase1 computed seq 0.
